metadata.title: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System

nodes.name: Tree Ensemble Model
nodes.statement: For a given data set with $n$ examples and $m$ features $\mathcal{D} = \{(\x_i, y_i)\}$ ($|\mathcal{D}| = n, \x_i\in \mathbb{R}^m, y_i \in \mathbb{R}$), a tree ensemble model~(shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:treemodel}) uses $K$ additive functions to predict the output. \begin{equation} \hat{y}_i = \phi(\x_i) = \sum^K_{k=1} f_k(\x_i), \ \ f_k\in \mathcal{F}, \end{equation} where $\mathcal{F}=\{f(\x) = w_{q(\x)}\} ( q : \mathbb{R}^m \rightarrow T, w\in \mathbb{R}^T) $ is the space of regression trees (also known as CART). Here $q$ represents the structure of each tree that maps an example to the corresponding leaf index.  $T$ is the number of leaves in the tree. Each $f_k$ corresponds to an independent tree structure $q$ and leaf weights $w$.

nodes.name: Regularized Learning Objective
nodes.statement: To learn the set of functions used in the model, we minimize the following \emph{regularized} objective. \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathcal{L}(\phi) =& \sum_{i} l( \hat{y}_i, y_i ) + \sum_{k}\Omega( f_{k} ) \\ \mbox{ where }& \Omega(f) = \gamma T + \frac{1}{2} \lambda \|w\|^2 \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Simplified second-order objective at step $t$
nodes.statement: We can remove the constant terms to obtain the following simplified objective at step $t$. \begin{equation} \tilde{\mathcal{L}}^{(t)} = \sum_{i=1}^n [g_i f_t(\x_i)+\frac{1}{2}h_i f_t^2(\x_i)] + \Omega(f_t) \end{equation}

nodes.name: Optimal weight $w_j^*$ of leaf $j$
nodes.statement: For a fixed structure $q(\x)$, we can compute the optimal weight $w_j^*$ of leaf $j$ by \begin{equation} w^*_j =-\frac{\sum_{i\in I_j} g_i}{\sum_{i\in I_j} h_i+\lambda}, \end{equation}

nodes.name: Structure score $\tilde{\mathcal{L}}^{(t)}(q)$
nodes.statement: and calculate the corresponding optimal  value by \begin{equation} \tilde{\mathcal{L}}^{(t)}(q) = - \frac{1}{2} \sum^T_{j=1}\frac{(\sum_{i\in I_j} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i\in I_j} h_i + \lambda}+\gamma T. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Loss reduction after split $\mathcal{L}_{split}$
nodes.statement: Assume that $I_L$ and $I_R$ are the instance sets of left and right nodes after the split. Lettting $I= I_L\cup I_R$, then the loss reduction after the split is given by \begin{equation} \mathcal{L}_{split} =\frac{1}{2} \left[\frac{(\sum_{i\in I_L} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i\in I_L} h_i + \lambda}+\frac{(\sum_{i\in I_R} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i\in I_R} h_i + \lambda} - \frac{(\sum_{i\in I} g_i)^2}{\sum_{i\in I} h_i + \lambda}\right] - \gamma \end{equation}

nodes.name: Exact Greedy Algorithm for Split Finding
nodes.statement: \KwIn{$I$, instance set of current node} \KwIn{$d$, feature dimension} $gain\leftarrow 0$\\ $G \leftarrow \sum_{i\in I} g_{i}$, $H \leftarrow \sum_{i \in I} h_{i}$\\ \For{$k=1$ {\bfseries to} $m$ }{ $G_L\leftarrow 0,\ H_L\leftarrow 0$\\ \For{$j $ in sorted($I$, by $\x_{jk}$)}{ $G_L\leftarrow G_L + g_j,\ H_L\leftarrow H_L + h_j$\\ $G_R\leftarrow G - G_L,\ H_R\leftarrow H - H_L$\\ $score \leftarrow \max(score, \frac{G_{L}^2}{H_{L}+\lambda} + \frac{G_{R}^2}{H_{R}+\lambda} - \frac{G^2}{H+\lambda})$\\ } } \KwOut{Split with max score}

nodes.name: Approximate Algorithm for Split Finding
nodes.statement: \For{$k=1$ {\bfseries to} $m$ }{ \mbox{Propose $S_k = \{s_{k1}, s_{k2}, \cdots s_{kl}\}$ by percentiles on feature $k$.}\\ \mbox{Proposal can be done per tree~(global), or per split(local).} } \For{$k=1$ {\bfseries to} $m$ }{ $G_{kv} \leftarrow = \sum_{j\in \{j| s_{k, v}\geq \x_{jk} > s_{k, v-1}\}} g_j$ $H_{kv} \leftarrow = \sum_{j\in \{j| s_{k, v}\geq \x_{jk} > s_{k, v-1}\}} h_j$ } Follow same step as in previous section to find max score only among proposed splits.

nodes.name: Weighted rank function $r_k$ and candidate split criteria
nodes.statement: Formally, let multi-set $\sD_k=\{(x_{1k}, h_1), (x_{2k}, h_2) \cdots (x_{nk}, h_n)\}$ represent the $k$-th feature values and second order gradient statistics of each training instances. We can define a rank functions $r_{k} : \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \Rplus$ as \begin{equation} r_{k}(z) =\frac{1}{\sum_{(x, h)\in \sD_k} h} \sum_{(x, h)\in \sD_k, x < z} h, \end{equation} which represents the proportion of instances whose feature value $k$ is smaller than $z$. The goal is to find candidate split points $\{s_{k1}, s_{k2}, \cdots s_{kl}\}$, such that \begin{equation} |r_{k}(s_{k,j})  - r_{k}(s_{k,j+1})| < \eps, \ \ s_{k1} = \min_i \x_{ik},  s_{kl} = \max_i \x_{ik}. \end{equation} Here $\eps$ is an approximation factor. Intuitively, this means that there is roughly $1 / \eps$ candidate points. Here each data point is weighted by $h_i$.

nodes.name: Sparsity-aware Split Finding
nodes.statement: \KwIn{$I$, instance set of current node} \KwIn{$I_k =\{i\in I|x_{ik} \neq \mbox{missing}\}$} \KwIn{$d$, feature dimension} \emph{Also applies to the approximate setting, only collect statistics of non-missing entries into buckets}\\ $gain\leftarrow 0$\\ $G \leftarrow \sum_{i\in I},  g_{i}$,$H \leftarrow \sum_{i \in I} h_{i}$\\ \For{$k=1$ {\bfseries to} $m$}{ \emph{// enumerate missing value goto right}\\ $G_L\leftarrow 0,\ H_L\leftarrow 0$\\ \For{$j $ in sorted($I_k$, ascent order by $\x_{jk}$)}{ $G_L\leftarrow G_L + g_j,\ H_L\leftarrow H_L + h_j$\\ $G_R\leftarrow G - G_L,\ H_R\leftarrow H - H_L$\\ $score \leftarrow \max(score, \frac{G_{L}^2}{H_{L}+\lambda} + \frac{G_{R}^2}{H_{R}+\lambda} - \frac{G^2}{H+\lambda})$\\ } \emph{// enumerate missing value goto left}\\ $G_R\leftarrow 0,\ H_R\leftarrow 0$\\ \For{$j $ in sorted($I_k$, descent order by $\x_{jk}$)}{ $G_R\leftarrow G_R + g_j,\ H_R\leftarrow H_R + h_j$\\ $G_L\leftarrow G - G_R,\ H_L\leftarrow H - H_R$\\ $score \leftarrow \max(score, \frac{G_{L}^2}{H_{L}+\lambda} + \frac{G_{R}^2}{H_{R}+\lambda} - \frac{G^2}{H+\lambda})$\\ } } \KwOut{Split and default directions with max gain}
output: Split and default directions with max gain

nodes.name: Time Complexity Analysis
nodes.statement: Let $d$ be the maximum depth of the tree and $K$ be total number of trees. For the exact greedy algorithm, the time complexity of original spase aware algorithm is $O(K d \|\x\|_0 \log n)$. Here we use $\|\x\|_0$ to denote number of non-missing entries in the training data. On the other hand, tree boosting on the block structure only cost $O(K d \|\x\|_0 + \|\x\|_0 \log n)$. Here $O( \|\x\|_0 \log n)$ is the one time preprocessing cost that can be amortized. This analysis shows that the block structure helps to save an additional $\log n$ factor, which is significant when $n$ is large. For the approximate algorithm, the time complexity of original algorithm with binary search is $O(K d \|\x\|_0 \log q)$. Here $q$ is the number of proposal candidates in the dataset. While $q$ is usually between 32 and 100, the log factor still introduces overhead. Using the block structure, we can reduce the time to $O(K d \|\x\|_0 + \|\x\|_0 \log B)$, where $B$ is the maximum number of rows in each block. Again we can save the additional $\log q$ factor in computation.

nodes.name: Quantile Summary (GK algorithm)
nodes.statement: One classical approach to this problem is GK algorithm~\cite{Greenwald:SIGMOID01} and extensions based on the GK framework~\cite{Zhang:SSDBM}. The main component of these algorithms is a data structure called quantile summary, that is able to answer quantile queries with relative accuracy of $\eps$.
nodes.origin_citation: Greenwald & Khanna, SIGMOD 2001 (GK algorithm); Zhang & Wang, SSDBM

nodes.name: Merge and prune operations for a quantile summary
nodes.statement: Two operations are defined for a quantile summary: \begin{itemize} \item A merge operation that combines two summaries with approximation error $\eps_1$ and $\eps_2$ together and create a merged summary with approximation error $\max(\eps_1,\eps_2)$. \item A prune operation that reduces the number of elements in the summary to $b+1$ and changes approximation error from $\eps$ to $\eps + \frac{1}{b}$. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Rank functions $r^-_{\sD}, r^+_{\sD}, \w_{\sD}, \w(\sD)$ for weighted data
nodes.statement: Given an input multi-set $\sD=\{(x_1,w_1), (x_2,w_2) \cdots (x_n,w_n)\}$  such that $w_i\in \Rplus, x_i \in \sX$. Each $x_i$ corresponds to a position of the point and $w_i$ is the weight of the point. Assume we have a total order $<$ defined on $\sX$. Let us define  two rank functions $r^-_{\sD}, r^+_{\sD}: \sX \rightarrow \Rplus$ \begin{equation} r^-_{\sD}(y) = \sum_{(x,w)\in \sD, x < y} w \end{equation} \begin{equation} r^+_{\sD}(y) = \sum_{(x,w)\in \sD, x \leq y} w \end{equation} We should note that since $\sD$ is defined to be a \emph{multiset} of the points. It can contain multiple record with exactly same position $x$ and weight $w$. We also define another weight function $\w_{\sD}:  \sX \rightarrow \Rplus$ as \begin{equation} \w_{\sD}(y) =  r^+_{\sD}(y)  - r^-_{\sD}(y) =  \sum_{(x,w)\in \sD, x = y} w . \end{equation} Finally, we also define the weight of multi-set $\sD$ to be  the sum of weights of all the points in the set \begin{equation} \w(\sD) = \sum_{(x,w)\in \sD} w \end{equation}

nodes.name: Quantile Summary of Weighted Data
nodes.statement: A quantile summary for $\sD$ is defined to be tuple $Q(\sD) = (S, \tdr^+, \tdr^-, \tdw)$, where $S = \{x_1, x_2,\cdots, x_k\}$ is selected from the points in $\sD$~(i.e. $x_i \in\{x|(x,w)\in \sD\}$) with the following properties: 1) $x_{i}< x_{i+1} \mbox{ for all } i$, and $x_1$ and $x_k$ are minimum and maximum point in $\sD$: $$x_1 = \min_{(x,w)\in \sD} x,\ \  x_k = \max_{(x,w)\in \sD} x$$ 2) $\tdr^+$, $\tdr^-$ and $\tdw$ are functions in $S\rightarrow \Rplus$, that satisfies \begin{equation} \tdr^-(x_i) \leq r^-_{\sD}(x_i),\ \  \tdr^+(x_i) \geq r^+_{\sD}(x_i), \ \ \tdw(x_i)\leq \w_{\sD}(x_i), \end{equation} the equality sign holds for maximum and minimum point~( $ \tdr^-(x_i) = r^-_{\sD}(x_i)$, $\tdr^+(x_i) = r^+_{\sD}(x_i)$ and $\tdw(x_i)= \w_{\sD}(x_i) $ for $i\in \{1, k\}$). \\ Finally, the function value must also satisfy the following constraints \begin{equation} \tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i)\leq \tdr^-(x_{i+1}), \ \ \tdr^+(x_i) \leq \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) \end{equation}

nodes.name: Extension of Function Domains
Extended Constraint
nodes.statement: The extended definition of $\tdr^-$, $\tdr^+$, $\tdw$ satisfies the following constraints \begin{equation} \tdr^-(y) \leq r^-_{\sD}(y),\ \  \tdr^+(y) \geq r^+_{\sD}(y), \ \ \tdw(y)\leq \w_{\sD}(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \tdr^-(y) + \tdw(y)\leq \tdr^-(x), \ \ \tdr^+(y) \leq \tdr^+(x) - \tdw(x), \mbox{ for all } y < x \end{equation}

nodes.name: $\eps$-Approximate Quantile Summary
nodes.statement: Given a quantile summary $Q(\sD) = (S, \tdr^+, \tdr^-, \tdw)$, we call it is $\eps$-approximate summary if for any $ y \in \sX$ \begin{equation} \tdr^{+}(y) - \tdr^{-}(y) - \tdw(y) \leq  \eps \w(\sD) \end{equation} We use this definition since we know that $r^-(y)\in[\tdr^{-}(y), \tdr^{+}(y) -\tdw(y)] $ and $r^+(y)\in[\tdr^{-}(y)+\tdw(y), \tdr^{+}(y)] $. Eq.~\eqref{eq:epsdef} means the we can get estimation of $r^+(y)$ and $r^-(y)$ by error of at most $ \eps \w(\sD)$.

nodes.name: Condition for $\eps$-approximate summary
nodes.statement: Quantile summary $Q(\sD) = (S, \tdr^+, \tdr^-, \tdw)$ is an $\eps$-approximate summary if and only if the following two condition holds \begin{equation} \tdr^{+}(x_i) - \tdr^{-}(x_i) - \tdw(x_i) \leq  \eps \w(\sD) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \tdr^{+}(x_{i+1}) - \tdr^{-}(x_i) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i}) \leq  \eps \w(\sD) \end{equation}

nodes.name: Combined summary additivity (merge)
nodes.statement: The combined quantile summary satisfies \begin{equation} \tdr^-(y) = \tdrx{1}^-(y) + \tdrx{2}^-(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \tdr^+(y) = \tdrx{1}^+(y) + \tdrx{2}^+(y) \end{equation} \begin{equation} \tdw(y) =\tdwx{1}(y)+ \tdwx{2}(y) \end{equation} for all $y\in \sX$

nodes.name: Merge preserves approximation error
nodes.statement: If $Q(\sD_1)$ is $\eps_1$-approximate summary, and  $Q(\sD_2)$ is $\eps_2$-approximate summary. Then the merged summary $Q(\sD)$ is $\max(\eps_1,\eps_2)$-approximate summary.

nodes.name: Query Function $g(Q,d)$
nodes.statement: \KwIn{$d$: $0 \leq d \leq \w(\sD)$} \KwIn{$Q(\sD) = (S, \tdr^+, \tdr^-, \tdw)$ where $S={x_1,x_2,\cdots,x_k}$} \lIf{$d < \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_1) + \tdr^+(x_1) ]$}{ \Return $x_1$ } \lIf{$d \geq \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_k) + \tdr^+(x_k) ]$}{ \Return $x_k$ } Find $i$ such that $\frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_i) ] \leq d < \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_{i+1}) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) ]$\\ \uIf{$ 2 d  < \tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) $} { \Return $x_i$ }\Else{ \Return $x_{i+1}$ }
output: a $x$ whose rank is close to $d$

nodes.name: Property of query function $g(Q,d)$
nodes.statement: For a given $\eps$-approximate summary $Q(\sD) = (S, \tdr^+, \tdr^-, \tdw)$, $x^*=g(Q,d)$ satisfies the following property \begin{equation} \begin{split} d &\geq \tdr^+(x^*) - \tdw(x^*) - \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD)\\ d &\leq \tdr^-(x^*) +\tdw(x^*) + \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) \end{split} \end{equation}

nodes.name: Prune preserves approximation error
nodes.statement: Let $Q'(\sD)$  be the summary pruned from  an $\eps$-approximate quantile summary $Q(\sD)$ with $b$ memory budget. Then $Q'(\sD)$ is a $(\eps+\frac{1}{b})$-approximate summary.
assumptions: $Q'(\sD)$  be the summary pruned from  an $\eps$-approximate quantile summary $Q(\sD)$ with $b$ memory budget

nodes.name: Proof of Extended Constraint
nodes.statement: The only non-trivial part is to prove the case when $y \in (x_i, x_{i+1})$: $$ \tdr^-(y) = \tdr^-(x_i)+\tdw(x_i) \leq r_{\sD}^-(x_i) +   \w_{\sD}(x_i) \leq  r_{\sD}^-(y) $$ $$ \tdr^+(y) = \tdr^+(x_{i+1})-\tdw(x_{i+1}) \geq r_{\sD}^+(x_{i+1}) - \w_{\sD}(x_{i+1}) \geq  r_{\sD}^+(y) $$ This proves Eq.~\eqref{eq:extend-1}. Furthermore, we can verify that $$ \tdr^+(x_{i}) \leq \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) =  \tdr^+(y) -\tdw(y) $$ $$ \tdr^-(y) +\tdw(y) = \tdr^-(x_i)+\tdw(x_i) + 0 \leq   \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) $$ $$ \tdr^+(y)= \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) $$ Using these facts and transitivity of $<$ relation, we can prove Eq.~\eqref{eq:extend-2}

nodes.name: Proof of condition for $\eps$-approximate summary
nodes.statement: The key is again consider $y\in(x_i, x_{i+1})$ $$ \tdr^{+}(y) - \tdr^{-}(y) - \tdw(y) =  [\tdr^+(x_{i+1})-\tdw(x_{i+1})]  - [ \tdr^+(x_{i})+\tdw(x_{i})] - 0 $$ This means the condition in Eq.~\eqref{eq:constraint2} plus Eq.\eqref{eq:constraint22} can give us Eq.~\eqref{eq:epsdef}

nodes.name: Proof that merge preserves approximation error
nodes.statement: For any $y\in \sX$, we have \begin{equation*} \begin{split} &\tdr^+(y) - \tdr^-(y) -\tdw(y)\\ =& [\tdrx{1}^+(y) +\tdrx{2}^+(y)] - [\tdrx{1}^-(y)+\tdrx{2}^-(y)] -[\tdwx{1}(y) + \tdwx{2}(y)]\\ \leq& \eps_1 \w(\sD_1)+\eps_2\w(\sD_2) \leq \max(\eps_1,\eps_2) \w(\sD_1\cup \sD_2) \end{split} \end{equation*} Here the first inequality is due to Lemma~\ref{lem:merge-extend}.

nodes.name: Proof of property of query function $g(Q,d)$
nodes.statement: We need to discuss four possible cases \begin{itemize} \item $d < \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_1) + \tdr^+(x_1) ]$ and $x^* = x_1$. Note that the rank information for $x_1$ is accurate ($\tdw(x_1) = \tdr^+(x_1) = \w(x_1)$, $\tdr^-(x_1)=0$), we have \begin{equation*} \begin{split} d &\geq 0 - \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) =  \tdr^+(x_1) - \tdw(x_1) - \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) \\ d &< \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_1) + \tdr^+(x_1) ]\\ &\leq \tdr^-(x_1) + \tdr^+(x_1)\\ &= \tdr^-(x_1) + \tdw^+(x_1) \end{split} \end{equation*} \item $d \geq \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_k) + \tdr^+(x_k) ]$ and $x^* = x_k$, then \begin{equation*} \begin{split} d &\geq \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_k) + \tdr^+(x_k) ]\\ & = \tdr^+(x_k) - \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^+(x_k) - \tdr^-(x_k)] \\ &= \tdr^+(x_k) - \frac{1}{2} \tdw(x_k)\\ d &< \w(\sD) + \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) = \tdr^-(x_k) +\tdw(x_k) + \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) \end{split} \end{equation*} \item $x^* = x_i$ in the general case, then \begin{equation*} \begin{split} 2 d  &<  \tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1})\\ &= 2[\tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i)] + [\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) - \tdr^-(x_i) - \tdw(x_i)]\\ &\leq 2[\tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i)] + \eps \w(\sD)\\ 2 d &\geq \tdr^-(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_i)\\ & = 2[ \tdr^+(x_i) - \tdw(x_i)] - [\tdr^+(x_i) - \tdw(x_i) - \tdr^-(x_i) ] + \tdw(x_i)\\ &\geq 2[ \tdr^+(x_i) - \tdw(x_i)] - \eps \w(\sD) + 0 \end{split} \end{equation*} \item $x^*=x_{i+1}$ in the general case \begin{equation*} \begin{split} 2 d  &\geq  \tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1})\\ &= 2[\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1})] \\ & \ \ \ \ -  [\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) - \tdr^-(x_i) - \tdw(x_i)]\\ &\geq 2[\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) + \tdw(x_{i+1})] - \eps \w(\sD)\\ 2 d & \leq \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1})\\ & = 2[ \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) + \tdw(x_{i+1})] \\ & \ \ \ \ + [\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) - \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) ] - \tdw(x_{i+1})\\ &\leq 2[ \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) + \tdw(x_{i+1})]  + \eps \w(\sD) - 0 \end{split} \end{equation*} \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Proof that prune preserves approximation error
nodes.statement: We only need to prove the property in Eq.~\eqref{eq:constraint2} for $Q'$. Using Lemma~\ref{lem:query}, we have \begin{equation*} \begin{split} \frac{i-1}{b}\w(\sD)   + \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD)  &\geq \tdr^+(x'_i) - \tdw(x'_i)\\ \frac{i-1}{b}\w(\sD)   - \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) &\leq \tdr^-(x'_i) +\tdw(x'_i) \end{split} \end{equation*} Combining these inequalities gives \begin{equation*} \begin{split} &\tdr^+(x'_{i+1}) - \tdw(x'_{i+1})  -  \tdr^-(x'_{i}) - \tdw(x'_{i}) \\ \leq& [ \frac{i}{b}\w(\sD) + \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD)] - [ \frac{i-1}{b}\w(\sD) - \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD)] = (\frac{1}{b} + \eps)\w(\sD) \end{split} \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Prove Eq. (extend-1) on the interval
nodes.statement: The only non-trivial part is to prove the case when $y \in (x_i, x_{i+1})$: $$ \tdr^-(y) = \tdr^-(x_i)+\tdw(x_i) \leq r_{\sD}^-(x_i) +   \w_{\sD}(x_i) \leq  r_{\sD}^-(y) $$ $$ \tdr^+(y) = \tdr^+(x_{i+1})-\tdw(x_{i+1}) \geq r_{\sD}^+(x_{i+1}) - \w_{\sD}(x_{i+1}) \geq  r_{\sD}^+(y) $$ This proves Eq.~\eqref{eq:extend-1}.

nodes.name: Prove Eq. (extend-2)
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we can verify that $$ \tdr^+(x_{i}) \leq \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) =  \tdr^+(y) -\tdw(y) $$ $$ \tdr^-(y) +\tdw(y) = \tdr^-(x_i)+\tdw(x_i) + 0 \leq   \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) $$ $$ \tdr^+(y)= \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) $$ Using these facts and transitivity of $<$ relation, we can prove Eq.~\eqref{eq:extend-2}

nodes.name: Case $x^*=x_1$
nodes.statement: $d < \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_1) + \tdr^+(x_1) ]$ and $x^* = x_1$. Note that the rank information for $x_1$ is accurate ($\tdw(x_1) = \tdr^+(x_1) = \w(x_1)$, $\tdr^-(x_1)=0$), we have \begin{equation*} \begin{split} d &\geq 0 - \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) =  \tdr^+(x_1) - \tdw(x_1) - \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) \\ d &< \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_1) + \tdr^+(x_1) ]\\ &\leq \tdr^-(x_1) + \tdr^+(x_1)\\ &= \tdr^-(x_1) + \tdw^+(x_1) \end{split} \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Case $x^*=x_k$
nodes.statement: $d \geq \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_k) + \tdr^+(x_k) ]$ and $x^* = x_k$, then \begin{equation*} \begin{split} d &\geq \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_k) + \tdr^+(x_k) ]\\ & = \tdr^+(x_k) - \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^+(x_k) - \tdr^-(x_k)] \\ &= \tdr^+(x_k) - \frac{1}{2} \tdw(x_k)\\ d &< \w(\sD) + \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) = \tdr^-(x_k) +\tdw(x_k) + \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) \end{split} \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Case $x^*=x_i$ (general)
nodes.statement: $x^* = x_i$ in the general case, then \begin{equation*} \begin{split} 2 d  &<  \tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1})\\ &= 2[\tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i)] + [\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) - \tdr^-(x_i) - \tdw(x_i)]\\ &\leq 2[\tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i)] + \eps \w(\sD)\\ 2 d &\geq \tdr^-(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_i)\\ & = 2[ \tdr^+(x_i) - \tdw(x_i)] - [\tdr^+(x_i) - \tdw(x_i) - \tdr^-(x_i) ] + \tdw(x_i)\\ &\geq 2[ \tdr^+(x_i) - \tdw(x_i)] - \eps \w(\sD) + 0 \end{split} \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Case $x^*=x_{i+1}$ (general)
nodes.statement: $x^*=x_{i+1}$ in the general case \begin{equation*} \begin{split} 2 d  &\geq  \tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1})\\ &= 2[\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1})] \\ & \ \ \ \ -  [\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) - \tdr^-(x_i) - \tdw(x_i)]\\ &\geq 2[\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) + \tdw(x_{i+1})] - \eps \w(\sD)\\ 2 d & \leq \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1})\\ & = 2[ \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) + \tdw(x_{i+1})] \\ & \ \ \ \ + [\tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) - \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) ] - \tdw(x_{i+1})\\ &\leq 2[ \tdr^-(x_{i+1}) + \tdw(x_{i+1})]  + \eps \w(\sD) - 0 \end{split} \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Apply query Lemma
nodes.statement: We only need to prove the property in Eq.~\eqref{eq:constraint2} for $Q'$. Using Lemma~\ref{lem:query}, we have \begin{equation*} \begin{split} \frac{i-1}{b}\w(\sD)   + \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD)  &\geq \tdr^+(x'_i) - \tdw(x'_i)\\ \frac{i-1}{b}\w(\sD)   - \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD) &\leq \tdr^-(x'_i) +\tdw(x'_i) \end{split} \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Combine inequalities
nodes.statement: Combining these inequalities gives \begin{equation*} \begin{split} &\tdr^+(x'_{i+1}) - \tdw(x'_{i+1})  -  \tdr^-(x'_{i}) - \tdw(x'_{i}) \\ \leq& [ \frac{i}{b}\w(\sD) + \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD)] - [ \frac{i-1}{b}\w(\sD) - \frac{\eps}{2} \w(\sD)] = (\frac{1}{b} + \eps)\w(\sD) \end{split} \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Initialize gain
nodes.statement: $gain\leftarrow 0$

nodes.name: Accumulate total statistics $G,H$
nodes.statement: $G \leftarrow \sum_{i\in I} g_{i}$, $H \leftarrow \sum_{i \in I} h_{i}$

nodes.name: Loop over features $k$
nodes.statement: \For{$k=1$ {\bfseries to} $m$ }

nodes.name: Reset left statistics
nodes.statement: $G_L\leftarrow 0,\ H_L\leftarrow 0$

nodes.name: Inner loop over sorted instances
nodes.statement: \For{$j $ in sorted($I$, by $\x_{jk}$)}

nodes.name: Update left statistics
nodes.statement: $G_L\leftarrow G_L + g_j,\ H_L\leftarrow H_L + h_j$

nodes.name: Update right statistics
nodes.statement: $G_R\leftarrow G - G_L,\ H_R\leftarrow H - H_L$

nodes.name: Update best score
nodes.statement: $score \leftarrow \max(score, \frac{G_{L}^2}{H_{L}+\lambda} + \frac{G_{R}^2}{H_{R}+\lambda} - \frac{G^2}{H+\lambda})$

nodes.name: Propose candidate split points
nodes.statement: \For{$k=1$ {\bfseries to} $m$ }{ \mbox{Propose $S_k = \{s_{k1}, s_{k2}, \cdots s_{kl}\}$ by percentiles on feature $k$.}\\ \mbox{Proposal can be done per tree~(global), or per split(local).} }

nodes.name: Aggregate bucket statistics
nodes.statement: \For{$k=1$ {\bfseries to} $m$ }{ $G_{kv} \leftarrow = \sum_{j\in \{j| s_{k, v}\geq \x_{jk} > s_{k, v-1}\}} g_j$ $H_{kv} \leftarrow = \sum_{j\in \{j| s_{k, v}\geq \x_{jk} > s_{k, v-1}\}} h_j$ }

nodes.name: Find max score among proposed splits
nodes.statement: Follow same step as in previous section to find max score only among proposed splits.

nodes.name: Initialize gain
nodes.statement: $gain\leftarrow 0$

nodes.name: Accumulate total statistics $G,H$
nodes.statement: $G \leftarrow \sum_{i\in I},  g_{i}$,$H \leftarrow \sum_{i \in I} h_{i}$

nodes.name: Loop over features $k$
nodes.statement: \For{$k=1$ {\bfseries to} $m$}

nodes.name: Enumerate missing value goto right
nodes.statement: \emph{// enumerate missing value goto right}\\ $G_L\leftarrow 0,\ H_L\leftarrow 0$\\ \For{$j $ in sorted($I_k$, ascent order by $\x_{jk}$)}{ $G_L\leftarrow G_L + g_j,\ H_L\leftarrow H_L + h_j$\\ $G_R\leftarrow G - G_L,\ H_R\leftarrow H - H_L$\\ $score \leftarrow \max(score, \frac{G_{L}^2}{H_{L}+\lambda} + \frac{G_{R}^2}{H_{R}+\lambda} - \frac{G^2}{H+\lambda})$\\ }

nodes.name: Enumerate missing value goto left
nodes.statement: \emph{// enumerate missing value goto left}\\ $G_R\leftarrow 0,\ H_R\leftarrow 0$\\ \For{$j $ in sorted($I_k$, descent order by $\x_{jk}$)}{ $G_R\leftarrow G_R + g_j,\ H_R\leftarrow H_R + h_j$\\ $G_L\leftarrow G - G_R,\ H_L\leftarrow H - H_R$\\ $score \leftarrow \max(score, \frac{G_{L}^2}{H_{L}+\lambda} + \frac{G_{R}^2}{H_{R}+\lambda} - \frac{G^2}{H+\lambda})$\\ }

nodes.name: Return $x_k$ if $d$ above range
nodes.statement: \lIf{$d \geq \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_k) + \tdr^+(x_k) ]$}{ \Return $x_k$ }

nodes.name: Locate bracketing index $i$
nodes.statement: Find $i$ such that $\frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_i) ] \leq d < \frac{1}{2}[\tdr^-(x_{i+1}) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) ]$

nodes.name: Return $x_i$ or $x_{i+1}$
nodes.statement: \uIf{$ 2 d  < \tdr^-(x_i) + \tdw(x_i) + \tdr^+(x_{i+1}) - \tdw(x_{i+1}) $} { \Return $x_i$ }\Else{ \Return $x_{i+1}$ }
